a2-unit-22.22.1 Kate and Pepper:
Kate: Rita! Hi! I haven't seen you for ages. When was it... eight months ago?
Rita: I think so. It was at the spring festival in the park. And who's this?
Kate: This is Pepper. I adopted her from an animal shelter three months ago.
Rita: Oh, she's beautiful! But a dog is a lot of work, isn't it? You're always so busy at the bakery.
Kate: I used to think that too. But honestly, Pepper has changed my life a lot. I used to work all day and then watch TV on the sofa every evening. Now I go out for walks with her two or three times a day.
Rita: Two or three times a day? When do you find the time?
Kate: Well, the problem was that I didn't use to have a good routine. Now I get up at six, we go for a long walk, and then I go to the bakery. I feel so much better.
Rita: I don't think I could do that. I'm at the coffee shop from seven in the morning, and I'm really tired when I get home. And who cleans up after her?
Kate: I do! That's part of the deal.
Rita: And dogs are expensive. There's the food, the vet...
Kate: Yes, they cost money. But spending time with her really helps me relax. I used to be so stressed. And Pepper has helped me make lots of new friends too. I didn't use to know any of my neighbors, but now everyone wants to stop and talk to me... well, to her!
Rita: That's so nice. You know, my grandmother had dogs all her life, and she lived to ninety-five.
Kate: Really? That makes sense. I read about a study from the American Heart Association. People with dogs had a lower risk of dying early.
Rita: Maybe I need a dog too! But I always sneeze when I'm near dogs. I think I'm a little allergic.
Kate: Oh no! What kind of dogs did your grandmother use to have?
Rita: Small ones. She used to have two at the same time, and they used to sleep on her bed!
